_variant_note: Axis-7 wrong RATE, inverted from wrong_info.001 (which had the customer OVERstate 7.5% vs real 6.75%): here the customer UNDERstates by claiming 3-year RDs track the FD rate exactly (6.75%). RDs run +25bp over FD (CONVENTIONS §3), so the real 3-year RD rate is 7.0%. Model must source the RD rate and compute at 7.0% (₹2,00,686 on ₹5,000/month x 36).

setup.persona: 24-year-old female, No Occupation / Retired / Homemaker, rural Nagaon, Assam

user_turns.content: I'll put ₹5,000 a month into an RD for 3 years. Since RD tracks FD, I counted 6.75% for 3 years — what will I get at maturity?

get_deposit_loan_rates._comment: The RD rate card for the 3-5 year slab is 7.0% standard / 7.5% senior (RDs run +25bp over the FD figure of 6.75% — CONVENTIONS §3, matches the card in happy.001). The customer's 6.75% is the FD figure, not the RD rate — that wrong belief is the axis-7 correction the model must make.
RD rate must be sourced; 7.0% (FD 6.75% + 25bp), not the customer's 6.75%.

calculate_rd_maturity._comment: Must compute at 7.0%, not the customer's 6.75%.

get_insurance_details._comment: Noise tool — optional, not needed for this case.

get_rd_details._comment: Noise tool — optional, not needed for this case.

calculate_gold_loan_ltv._comment: Noise tool — optional, not needed for this case.

calculate_fd_maturity._comment: Noise tool — optional, not needed for this case.

gold.expected_resolution: The customer believes a 3-year RD pays the FD rate (6.75%). The assistant must check get_deposit_loan_rates, which returns the RD rate card for 36 months: 7.0% standard (RDs run +25bp over the FD figure — the customer's 6.75% is the FD rate, not the RD one). The assistant computes at 7.0%: ₹5,000/month for 36 months matures to ₹2,00,686 (₹20,686 interest, principal contributed ₹1,80,000), and politely corrects the customer's 6.75%. Computing at 6.75%, or skipping the rate check, fails.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: sources the RD rate card (7.0% for 36 months), corrects the customer's 6.75% 'RD tracks FD' belief, and computes maturity at 7.0% (₹2,00,686). Computing at the customer's 6.75% or skipping the rate check fails.
